- Read docs/issue-1's discovery report and docs/issue-5's one-pager, and decided the job-fit question: algorithmic study-group matching (by course + exam date) is a **resolution-availability** feature, not the **monitoring** job issue #5 already committed to — the one-pager names this as an explicit, by-design scope exclusion, not an oversight.
- It also competes for the team's attention: it would inherit the "shared-ignorance ceiling" failure mode issue #1 documents for peer coping, and issue #5 already carries a registered, unrun falsifier for the monitoring bet itself (n=36, 6-week bound) that ranks higher by impact×risk.
- Registered a conditional hypothesis package (theory, 3 falsifiable hypotheses, metric/threshold/decision-rule/guardrail) for study-group matching in case the team revisits it later, per `product-discovery-hypothesis-preregistration` and `hypothesis-testing`.
- Recommendation: not now — run a zero-build check on whether existing tools (course Discords/GroupMes/LMS groups) already solve group coordination, and wait for issue #5's monitoring falsifier verdict before registering this for a real pilot.

## Summary

- Pre-registers the hypothesis package for the "02-onboarding-experiment" pilot: a redesigned first-run onboarding that mentions the comprehension-gap check, vs. the current onboarding that doesn't.
- Primary metric: 7-day check-completion rate (not screen-view or click-through, since the feature's mechanism only fires once a check is actually taken).
- Ship criterion: p<0.05 one-sided AND absolute lift >= 8 percentage points AND no guardrail breach.
- Sample size/duration: n=352 per arm (704 total), stopping rule = n reached or 8-week cap, no interim peeking.
- Guardrails: onboarding-funnel completion (>=3pp drop) and day-7 retention (>=2pp drop), both bounded and registered up front.

Closes #21

threshold.primary_metric: blind deliverable score margin (sum(skills-on) - sum(skills-off)) across registered pairs
threshold.decision_rule: better if skills-on wins >=3 of pairs AND combined margin >=3; worse under the symmetric condition; indistinguishable otherwise
threshold.sample_size_achieved: n=0 pairs with a completed paired comparison (0 of 2 registered pairs passed the H1 manipulation-check gate -- in both cases because the skills-off arm never dispatched, not because directive bytes matched under a completed run)
threshold.threshold_met_reason: not evaluable -- zero pairs produced a comparable skills-on/skills-off pair; see power_statement

decision: no pairs passed the H1 manipulation-check gate with a scored H2 -- nothing to compare against the pre-registered threshold. This is NOT the #3053 zero-mount failure mode (identical directive bytes from a corpus that leaked through); it is a distinct, newly-found dispatch-blocking defect (real, reproducible cross-family skill-source tier conflict, issue #2055's own fail-closed safety check) that prevented the skills-off arm from ever starting, for both registered pairs, on this execution machine.
power_statement: At the achieved n=0 completed paired comparisons (2 of 2 registered pairs excluded at the H1 gate), no directional read is possible at all -- the registered decision rule (>=3 of pairs won AND combined margin >=3) requires at least one scored pair to evaluate, and none exist. This is stronger than the pre-registration's own n=2 power statement ('cannot resolve an effect smaller than the registered 3-point margin'): at n=0, there is no resolution at any margin, in either direction. What WAS achieved: two real, independent skills-on sessions (issues #19, #21) each dispatched, ran to completion, and opened a real phase-1 PR, with real per-arm wall-clock (340.4s, 364.1s to PR-open), cost ($0.744, $0.806), turns (23, 29), and directive-composition-byte data reported above -- these are genuine H3-adjacent descriptive data points for the skills-on arm alone, but H3's own guardrail (skills-on vs skills-off wall-clock/verification-round comparison) is equally unevaluable with zero completed skills-off runs to compare against. Reporting 'not measured, manipulation check failed' per the operator's own framing for this exact all-pairs-fail case -- not a null, and not an indistinguishable-effect read; a distinct, dispatch-level blocker, with the actual stderr bytes and workspace byte counts recorded per pair above.
construct_validity_note_on_h1_metric: Independent of the dispatch-blocking defect: this session found that compute_h1_manipulation()'s chosen proxy (directive_composition_bytes, i.e. sum of <workspace>/.on-the-record/directive/*.md) would likely NOT have detected a genuine skills-on/skills-off difference even if the off arm had dispatched successfully. Both real skills-on workspaces (issues #19, #21) contain only the 8 session-universal baseline policy files in that directory (13026 bytes, identical across both) -- confirmed via the session logs (grep '"skill":"product-discovery-hypothesis-preregistration"' matches tool-call JSON, i.e. the skill is delivered at runtime via the Skill tool's on-demand invocation, not pre-written into a static per-skill directive file. A stub-vs-real skill corpus difference (frontmatter-only vs full procedure body) would show up in what the Skill tool *returns* when invoked, not in the pre-mounted directive file set this metric sums. This is a construct-validity gap in H1's operationalization for skill mounting mechanisms of this shape, separate from and in addition to the dispatch-blocking defect above -- flagged per experiment-trust's discipline of checking that a metric actually measures the manipulation it claims to gate, not assumed fixed here.
